'''Atul Gurtu''' (born 16 January 1946) is a [[high energy physics|high energy]] [[physicist]] in [[India]]. He joined the [[Tata Institute of Fundamental Research]] (TIFR), Mumbai, in 1971 and retired in 2011 as a senior professor, after a career spanning four decades in [[particle physics]] research.<ref name=cern>{{cite news |title=Faces and Places: Atul Gurtu retires from the Tata Institute |url=http://cerncourier.com/cws/article/cern/46059 |publisher=[[CERN Courier]]|date=6 June 2011}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Gurtu was born in [[Lahore]] in 1946.<ref name=toi>{{cite news |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/entertainment/hindi/bollywood/news/Suhasini-Mulay-ties-the-knot-at-60/articleshow/7669282.cms |title=Suhasini Mulay ties the knot at 60 |last=Shah |first=Kunal M. |work=[[The Times of India]] |date=11 March 2011}}</ref> Gurtu studied at Auckland House in [[Shimla]], and later at the [[Lawrence School Sanawar]] in [[Kasauli]]. He then attended [[Panjab University]] in [[Chandigarh]], obtaining his PhD in 1971, and thereafter joined the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (TIFR) in [[Mumbai]] in 1969.<ref name="today">{{cite web |url=https://www.indiatoday.in/magazine/science-and-technology/story/20110919-indian-scientists-at-forefront-of-research-atul-gurtu-747565-2011-09-10 |title=Back to Beginnings: Atul Gurtu |author=Nishat Bari |publisher=India Today |date=10 September 2011}}</ref>

==Career==
Gurtu is a [[particle physics]] researcher who participated in numerous experimental projects in collaboration with [[CERN]], Geneva, from 1969 to 2011, as part of the high energy physics group at TIFR.<ref name=cern/> From 2003 to 2011, he led a 70-member Indian team which participated in the CERN Compact Muon Solenoid (CMS) experiment at the [[Large Hadron Collider]].<ref name="researchgateprof">{{cite web |url=https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Atul-Gurtu |title=Atul GURTU - Senior Professor (Retd) - PhD - Tata Institute of Fundamental Research |publisher=ResearchGate |access-date=29 December 2025}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/mumbai/indian-scientists-play-key-role-in-god-particle-discovery/articleshow/15012345.cms |title=Indian scientists play key role in God particle discovery |work=The Times of India |date=5 July 2012}}</ref>

From 2011 to 2012, he was Distinguished Professor at [[King Abdulaziz University]], [[Jeddah]], Saudi Arabia. Since retiring from TIFR in 2011, he has continued contributions to the Particle Data Group collaboration.<ref name="researchgateprof" />

==Personal life==
Gurtu married Promila Bawa in 1971. They had one child, Ashish (1974–1991), who was disabled. Promila died in 2006.<ref name=toi/> In January 2011, he married [[National Film Award for Best Supporting Actress|National Film Award]]-winning actress [[Suhasini Mulay]], whom he met on [[Facebook]].<ref name=toi/>
